text: Create Accounting produces journal entries whether you look at them or not. This lesson is about actually looking: the screens and habits a consultant uses to inspect what SLA built, both to confirm it's correct and to investigate when something looks off.

Oracle Fusion provides a Review Journal Entries page where you search by ledger, subledger application, event class, date range, or batch. Opening an entry shows header info - accounting date, status, currency, the originating event - plus every line: account, debit or credit, the description your rule built, and any supporting references.

This page is where you confirm everything from chapters one through three actually worked: did the right lines generate, did they hit the right accounts, does the description read the way you intended, is the entry balanced.

One of the most useful habits: drilling in the opposite direction, from a GL journal entry back to the subledger transaction that generated it. Every subledger journal entry carries a reference to its origin, so Fusion supports drilling from the GL journal, through the subledger entry, to the actual source transaction.

This matters enormously. When a controller asks "why does this account have this balance," the answer is almost never visible from the GL journal alone - it's visible once you drill back through Subledger Accounting to the originating invoice, receipt, or asset transaction.

So remember: review entries on the Review Journal Entries page, and build the habit of drilling from GL back through SLA to the source. Reviewing routinely, not just reactively, catches mistakes early. Up next, lesson eighteen: accounting errors and corrections, what to do when that review finds something wrong.
